contract: F-13, the config/drive-release.json read contract and the field meanings every writer keeps (plan Appendix B, W-20; docs/app-updates.md §8.5, §5.10 table B.11, §5.1, §4.4, §2.5)

readers.readDriveRelease: readDriveRelease(rootPath) (src/main/services/updates/drive-release.ts): absent | unreadable (code: the errno token, never a message) | damaged (fault: not-a-file, empty, too-large, not-json, not-an-object) | record (appVersion, format, highestVersionSeen, each absent | invalid | valid with its value). Sync, never throws, no cache, logs nothing
readers.driveAppVersion: driveAppVersion(read): the only value a decision may use, the valid app_version or null (no constraint). `decision` in each read vector
readers.rootArtifactOf: rootArtifactOf(name, kind): the system and the carried version of one drive-root entry by release 1's root globs, or null. `artifacts`
readers.helper: node scripts/lib/write-drive-release.mjs --target <drive root> [--dry-run]: exit 0 written (or the dry run printed), 1 refused or failed (the old record untouched, no .tmp left), 2 usage. `tree`, `writes`, ../expected-record.json

parts: as f8-policy and f24-markers: a vector's bytes are its parts joined, `text` as UTF-8, `base64` decoded, `repeat` repeated `times` times. A byte-order mark and bytes that are not UTF-8 are held as base64: such bytes in a text file under tests/ fail the repo hygiene nets
at: where the vector's bytes go, under a scratch drive root that holds config/drive.json ({}): `file` (the default when `parts` is given) config/drive-release.json holds the parts; `no-config` no config folder at all; `absent` config/ exists, no record; `config-is-file` config is a regular file; `folder` a folder at the record's name; `file-link` a symbolic link to a file holding the parts (Windows: only with the symlink privilege); `dangling-link` a symbolic link to nothing (the same); `folder-link` a link to a folder (a junction on Windows, a symbolic link elsewhere); `config-link` config itself is such a link to a folder that holds drive.json; `fifo` a named pipe (macOS and Linux only); `deny-read` the file holds the parts and its reader is refused reading it; `held` (Windows only) the file holds the parts and another process holds it open with no sharing, as an antivirus scan does
shapes: `expect` is the reader's result exactly. A value is {"state":"absent"}, {"state":"invalid"} or {"state":"valid","value":…}. `codes`: an unreadable result's code is one of these (POSIX says EACCES, Windows EPERM). `anyOf`: either result is the contract (V8's JSON.parse decides; never a throw)

tree.why: the golden drive root: each path a file holding its ASCII text (no line end), folders implied. Recorded: the three root apps, the four start files, every regular file under runtime/. Never recorded: config/, models/, docs, logs/, workspace/, updates/, the root's other files, macOS litter

writes.why: each vector changes the golden tree (`remove` paths, `add` path → text; a folder at a path is made by adding a file inside it) and may put an existing record first (`existing`, parts). `record`: `golden` (byte for byte ../expected-record.json), an object (the parsed record: `app_version` a version or null when the field is omitted, `systems`, `paths` the files' paths in order when they differ from the golden's), `untouched` (the existing record's bytes) or `none` (no record). `append`: the golden's bytes with these lines between its files list and its closing brace (the kept fields, in order); `appendRepeat`: the same with one line `before` + `repeat` × `times` + `after`. `at` (as in `read`) places the existing record; `links`: a link at `at` to the folder or file `to` (both under the drive root), a folder link a junction on Windows, a file link needing the symlink privilege there. `dryRun`: run with --dry-run. `stdout`: the one line printed. `stderr`: words the one refusal or warning line holds
